concepts.claim: Movement choices and assessment depend on the intended skiing task and outcome.
concepts.sensor_transfer: Record intended task separately from descriptive sensor features.
limitations: Assessment guidance is not an experimentally validated scoring function.

concepts.claim: Outside-ski support is a coaching concept in parallel skiing and athlete development.
concepts.source_locator: Short-radius parallel turns; train-to-train technical guidance
concepts.sensor_transfer: Bilateral pressure sensing may investigate loading; boot inclination does not measure support force.
limitations: Visible posture cannot establish load distribution.
Insole measurements omit some boot-cuff force transmission.

concepts.claim: A dual-boot gyroscope method detected carved turns in field testing, with style-dependent limitations.
concepts.sensor_transfer: Prioritise replication with raw angular rates and independently annotated events.
limitations: Published validity does not establish single-boot MPU6050 validity.
Detection and event-time accuracy are different outcomes.

concepts.claim: An angulation drill uses deliberately exaggerated body movements to explore lateral balance.
concepts.sensor_transfer: No direct boot-only measurement of torso-leg angulation.
limitations: Drill hand positions must not become general technique targets.
The projected proxy is not an anatomical hip angle.

concepts.claim: Ski motion can include carving and skidding within the same turn.
concepts.sensor_transfer: Keep mixed and unknown labels; a boot inclination peak alone cannot establish a clean carve.
limitations: Race observations require separate validation for recreational skiing.

concepts.claim: A reference-based motion-quality scoring study did not discriminate all tested skill-group pairs.
concepts.sensor_transfer: Evaluate descriptive metrics and independent outcomes before developing a composite score.
limitations: Similarity to a selected reference group is not proof of effective technique.

concepts.claim: Bilateral boot reversal lag may describe coordination within matched parallel-turn tasks.
concepts.source_locator: Research motivation from bilateral sensing; this specific coaching claim is not established by the source
concepts.sensor_transfer: Requires two synchronised boot streams and consistent event definitions.
limitations: Zero lag is not an established ideal.
Clock error can imitate coordination differences.
Task and terrain can justify asymmetric movement.

error_hypotheses.description: Large upper-body changes may merit coach review when they coincide with an unintended turn outcome.
limitations: Terrain absorption and tactical movements can be appropriate.
Boot sensors cannot identify upper-body causes.

error_hypotheses.description: Timing variability may be informative during an explicitly constant-rhythm task.
limitations: Missed turn events inflate apparent variability.
